chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: The Benny Carter and Bob Freedman all-star band
summary: Freedman, a retired manufacturer, hired Carter's dream band with Carmen McRae, Joe Williams and Ernestine Anderson singing.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: But then I wanted -- did I mention the thing that I did with Benny and Bob Freeman? I did mention that, didn't
I? Yeah, but that was the -- personnel of that band -- I can't remember all of it but it was just a beautiful band.
I remember it, yeah.
That's right, you were there. And Carmen McRae sang some of the tunes and --
And Joe Williams sang.

Joe Williams sang some, and another girl, Ernestine Anderson, who I love. She sang some. I wonder what ever happened to her. She's a marvelous singer. I think she went back to Seattle. I hired her for a few jobs after that. I had -- casuals and I would always call her, because I enjoyed her singing so much.

Those were fabulous days (inaudible) Bob Freedman (maybe we should differentiate him from many other Bob Freedmans. This is the Bob Freedman who had no prior music reputation. He was a retired manufacturer --
Manufacturer, yeah.
-- who always wanted to be a song writer, and made enough money in bolt manufacturing or some kind of (metal) manufacturing.
Yeah, in Florida.
So that he could indulge himself. So he wrote songs and hired an absolute dream band.
That's right.
Was Benny doing all the (inaudible) and with arrangements
Yeah. Ray Brown was bass. Who played drums? Shelly Manne?
Shelly Manne and --
And Louie Bellson.
Bellson and Paul Humphreys.
Paul Humphreys, yeah, that's right, that's right. And the two guitarists, me and Barney Kessel. And Jimmy Jones, pianist, and --
It's like a Who's Who of Hollywood musicians.
That's right, it was just -- yeah, it was a beautiful, beautiful thing.
